rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies those upon whom the decree falls as the leaders.
rows.anchor: أي حقت عليهم كلمة العذاب وهم الرؤساء قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies them as the devils.
rows.anchor: قاله الكلبي. وقال قتادة: هم الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tempters say they led the followers astray as they themselves were astray.
rows.anchor: يعنون أضللناهم كما كنا ضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tempters and followers disavow one another; devils reject those who obeyed them and leaders reject those who accepted them.
rows.anchor: أي تبرأ بعضنا من بعض، والشياطين يتبرؤون ممن أطاعهم، والرؤساء يتبرؤون ممن قبل منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mutual enmity recalls the friends who become enemies on Judgment Day, except the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى: الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters are told to seek aid from the gods they worshipped in worldly life, asking them to rescue them from punishment.
rows.anchor: أي استغيثوا بآلهتكم التي عبدتموها في الدنيا لتنصركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call upon the gods for aid.
rows.anchor: فدعوهم } أي استغاثوا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gods neither answer nor benefit their worshippers.
rows.anchor: أي فلم يجيبوهم ولم ينتفعوا بهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the jawab of law is omitted: guidance would have saved them and kept them from punishment.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: جواب { لو } محذوف والمعنى: لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that, had they been guided, they would not have called upon the idols.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون ما دعوهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that, on seeing punishment, they wish they had followed guidance in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى: ودوا حين رأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks what answer they gave the prophets when they conveyed His messages.
rows.anchor: أي يقول الله لهم ما كان جوابكم لمن أرسل إليكم من النبيين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the proofs become hidden because God had already removed their excuse in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي خفيت عليهم الحجج قاله مجاهد لأن الله قد أعذر إليهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-anbāʾ means reports; their arguments are called reports because they are things they tell.
rows.anchor: الأخبار سمى حججهم أنباء لأنها أخبار يخبرونها

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says they do not ask one another about proofs because God has refuted their arguments.
rows.anchor: أي لا يسأل بعضهم بعضا عن الحجج لأن الله تعالى أدحض حججهم قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that they cannot utter an argument.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: { لا يتساءلون } أي لا ينطقون بحجة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view limits their silence to that terrifying moment; later they answer, as another report of their speech indicates.
rows.anchor: وقيل: { لا يتساءلون } في تلك الساعة، ولا يدرون ما يجيبون به من هول تلك الساعة

words: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story shows that Qarun possessed worldly adornment yet was not protected from punishment, like Pharaoh; it warns that the opponents are not richer or more numerous than they were.
rows.anchor: بين أن قارون أوتيها واغتر بها ولم تعصمه من عذاب الله

words: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى
rows.speaker: النخعي وقتادة وغيرهما
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, and others say Qarun was Moses’ paternal cousin; their genealogies meet at Qahith.
rows.anchor: قال النخعي وقتادة وغيرهما: كان ابن عم موسى لحا

words: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى
rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Qarun was Moses’ full paternal and maternal uncle.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: كان عم موسى لأب وأم

words: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes Qarun the son of Moses’ maternal aunt.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان ابن خالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun is indeclinable because it is a foreign proper name.
rows.anchor: ولم ينصرف للعجمة والتعريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Foreign masculine names on the fāʿūl pattern without a suitable definite article are indeclinable when definite but declinable when indefinite.
rows.anchor: وما كان على وزن فاعول أعجميا لا يحسن فيه الألف واللام لم ينصرف في المعرفة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Qarun would decline if derived from qarantu al-shayʾ.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: ولو كان قارون من قرنت الشيء لانصرف

rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab says Qarun’s transgression was letting his garment trail an extra span.
rows.anchor: بغيه أنه زاد في طول ثوبه شبرا قاله شهر ابن حوشب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report warns that God will not look at one who trails his garment out of arrogance.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: " لا ينظر الله إلى من جر إزاره بطرا "

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies Qarun’s transgression as disbelief in God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بغيه كفره بالله عز وجل قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Qarun wronged his people by despising them because of his abundant wealth and children.
rows.anchor: استخفافه بهم بكثرة ماله وولده قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says Qarun’s transgression was attributing God-given treasures to his own knowledge and ingenuity.
rows.anchor: نسبته ما أتاه لله من الكنوز إلى نفسه بعلمه وحيلته قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported story says Qarun resented Moses’ leadership and Aaron’s priestly role, demanded a sign, then dismissed Aaron’s staff sprouting leaves as magic.
rows.anchor: فقال لموسى: الأمر لكما وليس لي شيء إلى متى أصبر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Qarun paid a prostitute to accuse Moses of adultery; she confessed that Qarun had bribed her and Moses was innocent.
rows.anchor: قال سابع: روي عن ابن عباس قال: لما أمر الله تعالى برجم الزاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth obeys Moses’ command, swallowing Qarun little by little along with his house and companions while he calls for Moses.
rows.anchor: فجاءه وهو يقول للأرض: يا أرض خذيه وهي تأخذه شيئا فشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God tells Moses that his servants called on Moses without mercy, though they would have found God near and responsive.
rows.anchor: أوحى إلى موسى: استغاث بك عبادي فلم ترحمهم، أما أنهم لو دعوني

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Qarun and his people sink one stature each day and will not reach the earth’s bottom until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ابن جريج: بلغنا أنه يخسف بهم كل يوم قامة

rows.speaker: يونس بن ميسرة بن حلبس
rows.claim: Ibn Abi al-Dunya transmits from Yunus ibn Maysara that Qarun met Jonah in the sea’s darkness and urged him to repent; Qarun said his repentance had been entrusted to Moses, his cousin, who refused him.
rows.anchor: عن يونس بن ميسرة بن حلبس قال: لقي قارون يونس في ظلمات البحر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says Israfil will blow the Trumpet when Qarun reaches the seventh earth’s bottom.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر: إذا وصل قارون إلى قرار الأرض السابعة نفخ إسرافيل في الصور

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the prostitute was named Sabarta and Qarun paid her two thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: وكان اسم البغي سبرتا، وبذل لها قارون ألفي درهم

words: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Qarun crossed the sea with Moses, was called al-Munawwar for his handsome Torah description, but became a hypocrite like al-Samiri.
rows.anchor: قتادة: وكان قطع البحر مع موسى وكان يسمى المنور من حسن صورته في التوراة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAtaʾ says Qarun obtained many of Joseph’s treasures.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: أصاب كثيرا من كنوز يوسف عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الوليد بن مروان
rows.claim: Al-Walid ibn Marwan says Qarun practiced alchemy.
rows.anchor: وقال الوليد بن مروان: إنه كان يعمل الكيمياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle inna and its subject and predicate are within the relative clause of mā; mā is the object of ataynā.
rows.anchor: واسمها وخبرها في صلة { ما } و { ما } مفعولة

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas reports that ʿAli ibn Sulayman rejects the Kufans’ claim that inna and its governed phrase cannot form a relative clause, since the Qur’an has this construction.
rows.anchor: سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول ما أقبح ما يقول الكوفيون في الصلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mafātih is the plural of miftah, a key; if the singular is miftāḥ its plural is mafātīḥ.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع مفتح بالكسر وهو ما يفتح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mafātih means storehouses, its singular is maftaḥ with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: ومن قال هي الخزائن فواحدها مفتح بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best explanation is that the keys make the group lean under their weight; the wording shifts the preposition so the group appears to strain upward.
rows.anchor: أحسن ما قيل فيه أن المعنى لتنيء العصبة أي تميلهم بثقلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāʾa means to rise while bearing a heavy load.
rows.anchor: يقال: ناء ينوء نوءا إذا نهض بثقل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda reverses the construction: the group strains under the keys’ weight.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: قوله { لتنوء بالعصبة } مقلوب، والمعنى لتنوء بها العصبة

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd says nāʾtu bi-l-ḥiml means that I rose carrying the load.
rows.anchor: أبو زيد: نؤت بالحمل إذا نهضت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet’s line illustrates nāʾa as rising with difficulty under weight.
rows.anchor: تنوء بأخراها فلأيا قيامها وتمشي الهويني عن قريب فتبهر

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd cites a verse about a servant who stops when he bears a load, illustrating the usage nāʾa bi-l-ḥiml.
rows.anchor: إنا وجدنا خلفا بئس الخلف عبدا إذا ما ناء بالحمل وقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An additional usage, anāʾanī, means “made me heavy”.
rows.anchor: وأناءني إذا أثقلني عن أبي زيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another derivation connects the word to naʾy, distance; the cited poem uses yanʾawna for keeping away.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو مأخوذ من النأي وهو البعد

rows.speaker: بديل بن ميسرة
rows.claim: Badil ibn Maysara reads linūʾu with yāʾ, construing the singular understood referent as the subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بديل بن ميسرة: { لينوء } بالياء أي لينوء الواحد منها

rows.speaker: رؤبة بن العجاج
rows.claim: Ruʾba says his plural pronouns intentionally refer at once to the lines, their colors, and the combined image.
rows.anchor: فقال: أردت كل ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines ʿuṣba as three men.
rows.anchor: الأول: ثلاثة رجال قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to define it as three to ten people.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا من الثلاثة إلى العشرة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives the range fifteen to twenty for ʿuṣba.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: العصبة هنا ما بين العشرين إلى خمسة عشر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid is also reported to define it as ten to fifteen.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: ما بين العشرة إلى الخمسة عشر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A further report from Mujahid gives the range five to ten.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: من عشرة إلى خمسة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح والحكم بن عتيبة وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Abu Salih, al-Hakam ibn ʿUtayba, Qatada, and al-Dahhak define the group as forty men.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح والحكم بن عتيبة وقتادة والضحاك: أربعون رجلا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi defines ʿuṣba as ten to forty; Qatada is also reported to give this range.
rows.anchor: السدي ما بين العشرة إلى الأربعين. وقاله قتادة أيضا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says some define the group as forty and others as seventy.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: منهم من يقول أربعون، ومنهم من يقول سبعون

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi reports Abu Salih’s definition of ʿuṣba as seventy men.
rows.anchor: إن العصبة سبعون رجلا ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view defines the group as sixty men.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ستون رجلا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the group numbers six or seven.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد ابن جبير: ست أو سبع

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd defines ʿuṣba as three to nine, equivalent to nafar.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: ما بين الثلاثة والتسعة وهو النفر

rows.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say ʿuṣba means ten, citing Joseph’s brothers’ self-description.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عشرة لقول إخوة يوسف

rows.speaker: خيثمة
rows.claim: Khaithama says the Gospel described Qarun’s keys on sixty richly marked white camels; each key was finger-sized and opened a treasure sufficient for Basra.
rows.anchor: وقال خيثمة: وجدت في الإنجيل أن مفاتيح خزائن قارون وقر ستين بغلا غراء محجلة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the keys were made of camel hide.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: كانت المفاتيح من جلود الإبل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says the keys were made of cowhide to make them lighter.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من جلود البقر لتخف عليه

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says seventy mules carried Qarun’s keys when he rode.
rows.anchor: فيما ذكره القشيري

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak gives the number of mules carrying the keys as forty.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على أربعين بغلا. وهو قول الضحاك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says mafātih here means Qarun’s containers.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: إن مفاتحه أوعيته

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says mafātih means the treasure stores themselves.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال أبو صالح: إن المراد بالمفاتح الخزائن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the people who admonished Qarun as believing Israelites.
rows.anchor: أي المؤمنون من بني إسرائيل قاله السدي

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam identifies Qarun’s “people” here as Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن سلام: القوم هنا موسى

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the plural qawm can refer to one person, as in the verse about “the people” who spoke, meaning Nuʿaym ibn Masʿud.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: وهو جمع أريد به واحد كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here lā tafraḥ means do not exult arrogantly or act insolently.
rows.anchor: أي لا تأشر ولا تبطر

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi explain al-fariḥīn as the arrogant.
rows.anchor: أي البطرين قاله مجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem uses mufrāḥ for one who is not excessively elated when fortune favors him.
rows.anchor: ولست بمفراح إذا الدهر سرني ولا ضارع في صرفه المتقلب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Qarun is told not to rejoice in wealth because such joy does not lead him to fulfill its due.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: المعنى لا تفرح بالمال فإن الفرح بالمال لا يؤدي حقه

rows.speaker: مبشر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Mubashir ibn ʿAbd Allah interprets lā tafraḥ as “do not corrupt”.
rows.anchor: قال مبشر بن عبد الله: لا تفرح لا تفسد

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr says afraḥahu al-dayn means debt weighed him down, citing a poem about burdensome deposits.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: أفرحه الدين أثقله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says al-fariḥīn and al-fāriḥīn mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: والفرحين والفارحين سواء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ distinguishes the forms: al-fariḥīn are presently joyful, while al-fāriḥīn will rejoice later.
rows.anchor: وفرق بينهما الفراء فقال: معنى الفرحين الذين هم في حال فرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic phrase “you are dying and they are dying” contradicts al-Farraʾ’s analogy between mayyit and māʾit.
rows.anchor: ويدل على خلاف ما قال قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also interprets lā tafraḥ as “do not transgress,” and al-fariḥīn as aggressors.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا: معنى { لا تفرح } لا تبغ

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets the warning as “do not be miserly,” since God does not love misers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: لا تبخل إن الله لا يحب الباخلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use the worldly gifts God gave to seek Paradise, directing worldly means to the afterlife rather than tyranny.
rows.anchor: أي اطلب فيما أعطاك الله من الدنيا الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and most commentators say not to waste one’s lifetime without righteous works, since life and good deeds are one’s worldly share.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والجمهور: لا تضيع عمرك في ألا تعمل عملا صالحا

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say not to neglect lawful enjoyment, seeking it, or prudently considering worldly welfare.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: معناه لا تضيع حظك من دنياك في تمتعك بالحلال

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the softer reading allows the desired worldly good and avoids admonition so harsh that it alienates the addressee.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عطية

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar combines worldly and afterlife effort: cultivate worldly life as if living forever, and work for the afterlife as if dying tomorrow.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذان التأويلان قد جمعهما ابن عمر في قوله: احرث لدنياك كأنك تعيش أبدا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan advises giving away surplus while keeping what suffices.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن: قدم الفضل، وأمسك ما يبلغ

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says one’s worldly share is eating and drinking without extravagance.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: هو الأكل والشرب بلا سرف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the worldly share to remember is the shroud, since it is what remains of one’s possessions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بنصيبه الكفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first cited poem says that all one gathers leaves only two shrouds and embalming materials.
rows.anchor: نصيبك مما تجمع الدهر كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poem says the owner of all the world departs with nothing but cotton and a shroud.
rows.anchor: انظر لمن ملك الدنيا بأجمعها

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi calls Qatada’s reading best: one’s share of worldly life is its lawful portion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وأبدع ما فيه عندي قول قتادة: ولا تنس نصيبك الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing good as God did good means obeying and worshipping Him in response to His favor.
rows.anchor: أي أطع الله واعبده كما أنعم عليك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophetic definition of ihsan is to worship God as though one sees Him.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث: ما الإحسان؟ قال: " أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه "

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation makes the command an instruction to give alms to the poor.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو أمر بصلة المساكين

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says the many interpretations converge on using God’s blessings in obedience to Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: فيه أقوال كثيرة جماعها استعمال نعم الله في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says the command permits eating and drinking without extravagance.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: الأكل والشرب من غير سرف

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi reads Malik as answering excessive asceticism: the Prophet enjoyed sweets, honey, roast meat, and cold water.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: أرى مالكا أراد الرد على الغالين في العبادة والتقشف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking corruption in the land means committing sins.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعمل بالمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not love those who commit corruption.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يحب المفسدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun means knowledge of the Torah; he was reportedly among its most learned readers and one of the seventy chosen by Moses for the meeting.
rows.anchor: يعني علم التوراة. وكان فيما روي من أقرأ الناس لها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Qarun claimed God gave him wealth because God knew his merit and approved of him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أي إنما أوتيته لعلمه بفضلي ورضاه عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn Zayd’s reading, Qarun claims that God gave the treasures knowing he deserved them because of his virtue.
rows.anchor: معناه إن عندي أن الله تعالى آتاني هذه الكنوز على علم منه

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAli ibn ʿIsa says Qarun meant his own knowledge of trade and earning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أوتيته على علم من عندي بوجوه التجارة والمكاسب قاله علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun failed to recognize that his wealth could not have accumulated without God making acquisition easy.
rows.anchor: ولم يعلم أن الله لو لم يسهل له اكتسابها لما اجتمعت عنده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun meant his knowledge of making gold, referring to alchemy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: على علم عندي بصنعة الذهب

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash relates that Moses taught one third of alchemy to Qarun, who deceived Moses and Aaron to learn their portions and grew wealthy through it.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش: أن موسى عليه السلام علمه الثلث من صنعة الكيمياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Moses taught alchemy to Joshua, Caleb ibn Yufanna, and Qarun.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن موسى علم الكيمياء ثلاثة يوشع بن نون، وكالب بن يوفنا، وقارون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the Torah-knowledge explanation and rejects the alchemy explanation because alchemy is unreal.
rows.anchor: واختار الزجاج القول الأول، وأنكر قول من قال إنه يعمل الكيمياء.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further story says Moses taught alchemy to his sister, Qarun’s wife, who taught Qarun.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن موسى علم أخته علم الكيمياء، وكانت زوجة قارون

words: أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed generations were earlier unbelieving nations; Qarun should have known God destroys people stronger and wealthier than he.
rows.anchor: أي بالعذاب. { من القرون } أي الأمم الخالية الكافرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun’s predecessors had greater strength and amassed more wealth; if wealth proved merit, God would not have destroyed them.
rows.anchor: ولو كان المال يدل على فضل لما أهلكهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes strength as equipment and “gathering” as helpers and supporters.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القوة الآلات، والجمع الأعوان والأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a divine rebuke directed at Qarun.
rows.anchor: والكلام خرج مخرج التقريع من الله تعالى لقارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are not questioned to solicit an apology or satisfaction; they are instead rebuked and blamed.
rows.anchor: لا يسألون سؤال استعتاب كما قال: ولا هم يستعتبون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reconciles this with the statement that God will question everyone: questioning here is for rebuke, not to offer a chance to make amends.
rows.anchor: وإنما يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ لقوله: فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says angels will not need to ask about criminals, who are recognizable by their marks, including black faces and blue eyes.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: لا تسأل الملائكة غدا عن المجرمين فإنهم يعرفون بسيماهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says their sins are too obvious and numerous to require questioning, so they enter Hell without reckoning.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: لا يسأل المجرمون عن ذنوبهم لظهورها وكثرتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says criminals of this community are not questioned about the sins of earlier nations punished in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يسأل مجرمو هذه الأمة عن ذنوب الأمم الخالية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says God destroyed earlier peoples already knowing their sins, so He did not need to question them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أهلك من أهلك من القرون عن علم منه بذنوبهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says that after Moses ordered the earth to swallow Qarun, Israelites alleged Moses wanted his wealth; God swallowed Qarun, his house, and all his property after three days.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: لما أمر موسى الأرض فابتلعته قالت بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses that He will never again make the earth obey anyone after Moses.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى موسى إني لا أعيد طاعة الأرض إلى أحد بعدك أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasafa al-makān means a place disappeared into the earth; khasafa Allāhu bihi means God caused him to vanish into it.
rows.anchor: يقال: خسف المكان يخسف خسوفا ذهب في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording permits both “he sank into the earth” and “he was made to sink into it.”
rows.anchor: وخسف هو في الأرض وخسف به

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab says the best usage is that the sun is eclipsed and the moon sinks into eclipse.
rows.anchor: قال ثعلب: كسفت الشمس وخسف القمر هذا أجود الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasf can also mean diminution or a reduction one accepts.
rows.anchor: والخسف النقصان يقال: رضي فلان بالخسف أي بالنقيصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiʾa means a group or band.
rows.anchor: أي جماعة وعصابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muntaṣirūn means those able to protect themselves from the sinking that befell them.
rows.anchor: أي الممتنعين فيما نزل به من الخسف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says Qarun sinks one stature each day until reaching the lowest earth, when Israfil blows the Trumpet.
rows.anchor: فيروى أن قارون يسفل كل يوم بقدر قامة، حتى إذا بلغ قعر الأرض السفلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who had wished for Qarun’s place now regret having wished for it.
rows.anchor: أي صاروا يتندمون على ذلك التمني

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه ويونس والكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, Yunus, and al-Kisaʾi explain way as a regretful exclamation when people awaken or are made to notice.
rows.anchor: أحسن ما قيل في هذا قول الخليل وسيبويه ويونس والكسائي

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari says way is an exclamation, used in expressions such as wayka and way to ʿAbd Allah.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري: وي. كلمة تعجب، ويقال: ويك ووي لعبد الله

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil separates the expression as way followed by an independently begun kaʾanna.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل: هي مفصولة تقول: { وي } ثم تبتدىء فتقول: { كأن }

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats it as an affirming expression, like “do you not see” God’s action and generosity.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء هي كلمة تقرير كقولك: أما ترى إلى صنع الله وإحسانه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan take wayka as an opening affirmation: God indeed expands provision.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن: ويك كلمة ابتداء وتحقيق تقديره: إن الله يبسط الرزق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view treats it as an attention-getter like alā or ammā baʿd.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو تنبيه بمنزلة ألا في قولك ألا تفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem about a divorce uses way as a regretful exclamation.
rows.anchor: وي كأن من يكن له نشب يحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem uses wayka in a statement about wealth and poverty.
rows.anchor: وي كأن من يكن له نشب يحب

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub derives waika from waylaka with the lām dropped and the address kāf joined to way.
rows.anchor: قال قطرب: إنما هو ويلك وأسقطت لامه وضمت الكاف

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: ʿAntara’s line uses wayka as an address, illustrating Qutrub’s proposed construction.
rows.anchor: وأنكره النحاس وغيره، وقالوا: إن المعنى لا يصح عليه

rows.speaker: النحاس وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas and others reject Qutrub’s derivation: the speakers address no one, the resulting sense is wrong, and dropping lām from waylaka is impermissible.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: التقدير ويلك اعلم أنه فأضمر اعلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis supplies an omitted command: “waylaka, know that …”.
rows.anchor: ابن الأعرابي: { ويكأن الله } أي اعلم

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi glosses waykaʾanna as “know”.
rows.anchor: ابن الأعرابي: { ويكأن الله } أي اعلم. وقيل: معناه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss is “do you not see that God …”.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ألم تر أن الله

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says the phrase means “mercy to you” in the language of Himyar.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: وي فيه معنى التعجب. ويروى عنه أيضا الوقف على وي

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says way expresses wonder and is also transmitted as a pause expressing grief.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: ويك فوقف على الكاف فمعناه أعجب لأن الله يبسط الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one pauses after the kāf in waika, it expresses wonder at God expanding provision and at unbelievers not prospering.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: ويك فوقف على الكاف فمعناه أعجب لأن الله يبسط الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf is an address particle, not a noun, because way cannot enter a genitive construction; frequent use explains the connected spelling.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن تكون الكاف حرف خطاب لا اسما لأن وي ليست مما يضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they would have been swallowed too, had God favored them with faith and mercy and guarded them from Qarun’s arrogance.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش { لولا من الله علينا }

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads lawlā man allāhu ʿalaynā, omitting an.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص: «لخسف بنا» مسمى الفاعل

rows.speaker: حفص
rows.claim: Hafs reads lakhusifa bina with the verb active.
rows.anchor: الباقون: على ما لم يسم فاعله وهو اختيار أبي عبيد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the passive, which Abu ʿUbayd selects.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله { لانخسف بنا } كما تقول انطلق بنا. وكذلك قرأ الأعمش وطلحة بن مصرف

rows.speaker: عبد الله والأعمش وطلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allah and readings of al-Aʿmash and Talha ibn Musarrif have lanakhsif bina, “we would sink”.
rows.anchor: واختار قراءة الجماعة أبو حاتم لوجهين: أحدهما قوله: { فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض }

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim chooses the majority reading because the preceding verse says “We caused him and his house to sink,” and the nearby mention of God favors attribution to Him.
rows.anchor: والثاني قوله: { لولا أن من الله علينا } فهو بأن يضاف إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim’s second reason is that the nearby clause says God favored them, making divine attribution apt.
rows.anchor: والثاني قوله: { لولا أن من الله علينا } فهو بأن يضاف إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final statement means that disbelievers do not prosper with God.
rows.anchor: عند الله

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi parses Ibrāhīm as accusative governed by anja(y)nâ, coordinated with the pronoun in “We saved”.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: { وإبراهيم } منصوب ب { أنجينا } يعني أنه معطوف على الهاء

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi also allows coordination with Nuh, yielding “and We sent Abraham”.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي أن يكون معطوفا على نوح، والمعنى وأرسلنا إبراهيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third parsing makes Ibrāhīm accusative under an implied “remember”.
rows.anchor: وقول ثالث: أن يكون منصوبا بمعنى واذكر إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham tells his people to worship God alone.
rows.anchor: أي أفردوه بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them to fear God’s punishment and torment.
rows.anchor: أي اتقوا عقابه وعذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping God and fearing Him is better than worshipping idols, if they know.
rows.anchor: أي من عبادة الأوثان { إن كنتم تعلمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awthān means idols.
rows.anchor: أي أصناما

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda distinguishes ṣanam, made of gold, silver, or copper, from wathan, made of plaster or stone.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الصنم ما يتخذ من ذهب أو من فضة أو نحاس

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari says wathan means ṣanam and gives its plural as awthān.
rows.anchor: الجوهري: الوثن الصنم والجمع وثن وأوثان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads takhluqūn as carving: they worship idols that they themselves manufacture.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: معنى: { تخلقون } تنحتون فالمعنى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says ifk means a lie: they worship idols and fabricate falsehood.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الإفك الكذب، والمعنى تعبدون الأوثان وتخلقون الكذب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman has a reading of the verb recorded as wa-takhluqūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن: { وتخلقون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two further forms are reported: one intensive form of khalaqa, and one from takhallaqa meaning to lie or invent.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: { تخلقون } بمعنى التكثير من خلق و { تخلقون } من تخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afkan has two analyses: a verbal noun like kadhib or laʿib, with ifk as its lightened form; or an adjective meaning a false creation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: { أفكا } وفيه وجهان: أن يكون مصدرا نحو كذب ولعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awthānan is the object of taʿbudūna, and mā is an inna-blocking particle.
rows.anchor: و { أوثانا } نصب ب { تعبدون } و { ما } كافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outside the Qur’anic reading, awthān may be nominative if mā is taken as inna’s noun, taʿbudūn as its relative clause, and awthān as its predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز في غير القرآن رفع أوثان على أن تجعل { ما } اسما لأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase wa-takhluqūna ifkan is accusative through the verb alone.
rows.anchor: فأما { وتخلقون إفكا } فهو منصوب بالفعل لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot provide sustenance; direct hopes and requests for provision to God alone.
rows.anchor: أي اصرفوا رغبتكم في أرزاقكم إلى الله فإياه فاسألوه وحده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view makes this Abraham’s speech: unbelief is a recurring habit among disbelievers, and messengers are responsible only for conveying the message.
rows.anchor: أي التكذيب عادة الكفار وليس على الرسل إلا التبليغ

words: أولم يروا كيف يبديء الله الخلق
rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The general reading has the third-person yāʾ; Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim prefer it because “the nations” were just mentioned.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة بالياء على الخبر والتوبيخ لهم، وهي اختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayd explains the third-person plural by taking the previously mentioned nations as the subject.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: لذكر الأمم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر والأعمش وابن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Abu Bakr, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Waththab, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read taraw with second-person address, linked to “if you disbelieve”.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر والأعمش وابن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the address “if you disbelieve” is to Quraysh rather than part of Abraham’s speech.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر والأعمش وابن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي: { تروا } بالتاء خطابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return of creation means resurrection.
rows.anchor: { ثم يعيده } يعني الخلق والبعث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is the recurring life, death, and return of fruits; humans likewise reproduce through successive generations, as do other animals.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أولم يروا كيف يبدىء الله الثمار فتحيا ثم تفنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing God originate creation proves He can recreate it; this is easy for Him, who brings about what He wills by saying “Be”.
rows.anchor: فإذا رأيتم قدرته على الإبداء والإيجاد فهو القادر على الإعادة
